content.title: About
content.content: Pie, oatmeal is a baked dessert made from a crust and a filling of oatmeal, milk, eggs and sugar. Often fruit, nuts or spices are added. The result is a tender crumb with a fragrant, mildly sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oat flakes in the filling make the pie more nutritious and give it a characteristic nutty aroma.
Traditionally this pie is prepared in the autumn, when oats are harvested in large quantities.
In some regions honey is used instead of sugar in the dough, adding a distinct taste note.
Oatmeal pie is commonly served with tea or coffee as a light dessert.
Oats are considered a symbol of abundance and well‑being in several cultures.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Oat flakes provide soluble and insoluble fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of slow‑release carbs
items.content: The starch in oats is released gradually, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains beta‑glucans
items.content: Beta‑glucans can lower cholesterol and support the immune system.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Oats supply B1, B5 and folate, essential for metabolic processes.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The pie provides magnesium, iron and zinc, which aid muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: If wheat flour is used in the crust, the product may be unsafe for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweet versions can contribute to weight gain when consumed in excess.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: The crust and butter make the pie calorie‑dense, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Added additives
items.content: Some recipes include artificial flavors or preservatives that may trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the oatmeal pie warm or at room temperature. It can be enjoyed on its own or paired with yogurt, fresh berries or ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the pie in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage refrigerate up to 5 days, or freeze and reheat in the oven before serving.
